rationale:
In build_closing_bracket_map, return an empty dict immediately if the source contains no '[' (a cheap substring test). Since the order lens does not really apply to this hot path, this is stated as a plain shortcut. Additionally, the dict's insertion order (closing order) is never relied on for output, so it may be built in any order.
Why it should win: build_closing_bracket_map has 4031 calls and 4.2% self time, scanning char by char in Python. Many sources reached through the link/label_contai

ns_link path may contain few brackets; a substring test is far cheaper than the loop.
Precondition: The map is only consulted via .get(pos) and .items() to build ranges that are sorted afterwards, so dict order does not affect results. A source without '[' yields an empty map.
What the relaxed rule changes: The output is identical: with no '[' the loop never pushes onto the stack so the map is empty anyway. Dict iteration order is re-sorted in get_link_range_index, so no visible order changes.
title: Skip building the closing-bracket map when a text has no '[' character

rationale:
Build, lazily or when the renderer is finalized by Markdown.__init__, a dict from token type to bound method, covering the class's public render methods and the registered plugin methods. Invalidate it in register(). render_token then does one dict lookup instead of calling _get_method with object.__getattribute__ and try/except. The dict could be generated once per renderer instance and shared across calls.
Why it should win: render_token and _get_method run 91,619 times each, with a combined s

elf time of about 6%. A dict lookup per token removes one Python call frame and the attribute-resolution cost per token.
Precondition: Render methods are not monkeypatched on the instance after the first render without register(); the table is rebuilt whenever register is called.
What the relaxed rule changes: The same bound method is resolved for every token type, so output is identical. Unknown types still raise the same AttributeError by falling back to the old path.
title: Precompute per-token-type renderer dispatch table at renderer setup, bypassing _get_method

rationale:
Change InlineParser.parse so that, when the source contains none of the trigger characters, it returns early with a single text token. Add a public helper that checks the source once with the compiled trigger regex, and have parse return the token list directly without running the scan loop or the emphasis finalizer. Callers that rely on state.tokens being set must read the return value instead.
Why it should win: parse has 18683 calls and _find_fast_text_end 55819 calls, so many short plain-tex

t sources pass through the full loop and finalize_emphasis_tokens. A single up-front trigger search lets plain sources bypass the loop.
Precondition: Fast trigger chars must be available (all rules known). Callers of parse must use its return value, not state.tokens, for the plain-text case.
What the relaxed rule changes: A source with no trigger chars yields exactly one text token, the same as the current pos==0 special case. Output HTML is unchanged. The API change is that state.tokens may sta
y empty for such sources.

label: relax_api

rationale:
Add the third-party 'regex' package and compile the whole SQL_REGEX table into one alternation with named or numbered branches, keeping the original priority order. Scan with a single finditer-style pass instead of trying each compiled pattern at every position. Keep the keyword-callback and Error-token fallback, and map the matched branch back to its action.
Why it should win: get_tokens is the top self-time hotspot (9.9%, 66k calls). For each position it loops over dozens of compiled regexes v

ia Python, plus enumerate and consume overhead. One combined pattern moves the dispatch into C.
Precondition: The dependency check must allow adding the 'regex' package. Every SQL_REGEX entry must work in a combined alternation: no group-number-dependent backreferences, and the same IGNORECASE and UNICODE flags for all. The first-match alternation order must reproduce the original ordered-try semantics.
What the relaxed rule changes: The token stream is identical because alternation tries branch
es in the same order as the original loop, and unmatched characters still yield Error tokens. Users get a new runtime dependency.
title: Replace per-character regex-table lexer loop with a single combined regex scanner via the 'regex' package

rationale:
Compile sqlparse/utils.py and the Token and TokenList classes in sql.py into native extensions (mypyc or Cython in pure-Python mode) as an optional build, falling back to the Python sources. Add type annotations to imt, Token.match and TokenList._token_matching so the generated code avoids dynamic dispatch.
Why it should win: imt (524k calls), Token.match (751k calls), _token_matching and the lambda wrapper together take about 25% self-time, all in tiny Python functions where call overhead domin

ates. Compiling removes interpreter overhead without changing the algorithms.
Precondition: The dependency check must allow a build-time compiler dependency (mypyc or Cython) and a compiled artifact in the environment. The classes must stay subclassable and compatible with __slots__ and the existing public API.
What the relaxed rule changes: The compiled code runs identical logic, so results are the same. The user must install a compiled build, and a pure-Python fallback is kept.
title: Compile the lexer hot loop and token-list helpers with mypyc or Cython-compiled extension modules

rationale:
Generate at install or build time a module that holds, for each possible leading character class, the ordered sublist of SQL_REGEX entries that can match there. Lexer.set_SQL_REGEX loads this table, and get_tokens looks up the sublist by the current character instead of trying every compiled regex in turn. Keep the original order within each sublist, and fall back to the full list for characters not in the table.
Why it should win: get_tokens is the top hotspot at about 10% self time with 66k ca

lls. For every position it tries regexes in order, and most fail at once. A precomputed table removes most failed match calls per token.
Precondition: The install step may run a generator script and ship the generated table. The table must be rebuilt whenever SQL_REGEX changes. It must be computed conservatively: a regex is excluded for a character only if it provably cannot match starting with that character. Custom regexes set by the user must fall back to the full list.
What the relaxed rule

changes: Each position still tries, in the original order, every regex that could match, so the first match and the token stream are identical. For users, the package gains a generated file, and the table is skipped when the regex list is customised.
title: Build-time combined lexer regex with first-character dispatch table generated at install

rationale:
Change the public signature of TokenList.token_next_by so a caller may pass a ready-made predicate (or precompiled matcher object) instead of i/m/t. Grouping functions such as group_identifier, group_functions, group_where and group_order build the predicate once per call and reuse it inside their while loops. Callers outside the library that use i/m/t keyword arguments would still work.
Why it should win: imt is called 524k times and the lambda in token_next_by 435k times; each loop iteration i

n the group_* functions rebuilds a lambda and re-dispatches on isinstance/list checks inside imt. A prebuilt predicate removes this work.
Precondition: Callers of token_next_by in the repo can be edited; external users keep working through the old keyword arguments, which stay supported.
What the relaxed rule changes: Output is identical. Only an added optional argument is visible to users; the existing i/m/t behaviour is unchanged.
title: Let token_next_by accept a prebuilt predicate to avoid per-call lambda and imt dispatch

rationale:
Change _group_matching so it takes a list of group classes and handles brackets, parenthesis, case, if, for and begin in one traversal with one stack per class. group_brackets, group_parenthesis and the others become thin wrappers or are removed from group()'s list. Each token list is then visited once instead of six times.
Why it should win: _group_matching is called 9.8k times, with each call re-listing tokens and calling token.match twice per non-whitespace token (751k match calls overall). M

erging the six passes cuts the per-token match calls and the recursion into sub-groups.
Precondition: The pass order has no observable interplay between the classes. This must be checked, because a Case inside a Parenthesis depends on the parenthesis having been grouped first.
What the relaxed rule changes: The tree must be identical. The risk is ordering differences in nested groups, so a behaviour check against the existing tests is needed. The public group_* helper functions would change sign
ature or disappear.
title: Single-pass grouping API: change group() to run matching passes with a shared pre-scan of token kinds

rationale:
Add a lexer entry point that yields sql.Token objects directly, and change StatementSplitter.process to accept them. This removes one tuple allocation and unpack per token and lets the splitter use the token's cached is_keyword, normalized and is_whitespace attributes in place of repeated ttype containment and value.upper() calls. The public tokenize() keeps returning tuples.
Why it should win: The splitter handles every token and calls ttype containment, .upper() and .split() per keyword, while

Token.__init__ already computes these. Computing them once removes duplicate work (__contains__ is called 499k times).
Precondition: StatementSplitter.process's input type may change; FilterStack is its only internal caller, and external callers of the splitter must adapt to token objects.
What the relaxed rule changes: Parsed output is identical. Anyone calling StatementSplitter.process with raw tuples would need to pass Token objects, or use a new method.

label: relax_api

rationale:
Add the 'regex' package as a dependency. Where inline patterns compile their regexes, have getCompiledRegExp use regex.compile instead of re.compile, with the same flags, so finditer in __applyPattern runs on the faster engine.
Why it should win: __applyPattern is the top hotspot (16.8% self time, 233k calls), and each call runs a finditer over short text. Regex engine speed bounds this cost. The gain is uncertain: the regex module is often not faster than re on simple patterns and has higher pe

r-call overhead.
Precondition: The rule against new dependencies must be lifted to allow 'regex'. All inline patterns must behave identically under regex semantics, including Unicode flags, lookbehinds and backtracking.
What the relaxed rule changes: Output is intended to be identical. Users would gain an installation requirement on 'regex'. Subtle differences in Unicode case folding or \b semantics could change matches in rare inputs, so the change needs verification against the full test suite
title: Use the third-party 'regex' module to compile inline patterns for faster scanning in __applyPattern

rationale:
In InlineProcessor.run, take a snapshot list of the inline patterns (via iteration of the registry) once per run and use that list for indexing in __handleInline and the length check, instead of going through Registry.__getitem__ and len on every loop step. The order in which patterns are applied is unchanged, but the processing order of siblings/tree nodes may differ if combined with a deque or LIFO traversal.
Why it should win: Registry.__getitem__ is 7% self time with 237k calls, nearly one p

er __applyPattern call; each call runs _sort, isinstance checks and two lookups.
Precondition: Inline patterns are not registered or deregistered while run() executes (true for built-in patterns; an extension altering them mid-run would break).
What the relaxed rule changes: Same patterns in same priority order are applied to every string, so the HTML output is identical. The relaxed output-order rule is not actually needed here.
title: Cache inline pattern registry as a plain list once per run, bypassing Registry.__getitem__ sorting

rationale:
Keep a materialised list of the registered items in priority order, built once at the first read after any register or deregister (or at the end of Markdown construction). Integer-key __getitem__ then returns that list element directly, without calling _sort, building a _PriorityItem lookup or doing the second dict lookup. Invalidate the list in register and deregister.
Why it should win: Registry.__getitem__ runs 237k times for 7.2% self time. Nearly all calls are integer indexing of inlinePatt

erns from __handleInline. Each call does a _sort call, an isinstance(slice) check, an isinstance(int) check, a priority index, a name attribute lookup and a dict lookup.
Precondition: All mutation of the registry goes through register and deregister, so the cached list can be invalidated there. No code writes to _data or _priority directly; this must be checked, including in extensions.
What the relaxed rule changes: The returned items and their order are identical. Name and slice keys behave as
before. Only the lookup path for integer keys is shorter, so the HTML output is byte-identical.
title: Cache Registry sorted snapshot as a list so InlineProcessor indexing skips _sort and dict lookups

rationale:
At InlineProcessor setup, or lazily once per pattern object, cache for each pattern a flag for whether it is the new-style class and a tuple of lowercased ancestor excludes. In __applyPattern use the cache, so the isinstance check and the per-call exclude.lower() calls disappear, and the common case of no excludes costs one truthiness test.
Why it should win: __applyPattern is called 233k times and is the top self-time hotspot at 16.8%. Each call runs isinstance on the pattern class and iterates

ANCESTOR_EXCLUDES, calling lower() on every entry for patterns that define excludes, such as the link patterns.
Precondition: ANCESTOR_EXCLUDES is not mutated after registration, and pattern classes are not swapped at run time. The cache must be keyed per pattern object, and invalidating it must be possible if an extension changes the registry.
What the relaxed rule changes: The same exclusion decision is made with the same lowercase comparison, and the same early-return tuple results. Output i
s unchanged.
title: Precompute per-pattern ANCESTOR_EXCLUDES lowercase tuples and skip empty check in __applyPattern

rationale:
Give InlineProcessor a snapshot tuple of the sorted patterns, built once at the start of run(), and have __handleInline index that tuple instead of calling Registry.__getitem__ (which calls _sort and does a dict lookup on every pattern step). The public change: Registry-like objects used for inlinePatterns need a documented way to produce a frozen ordered list, and extensions that register patterns during run() would no longer be seen mid-run.
Why it should win: Registry.__getitem__ is called 23

7k times costing 7% self time plus call overhead; __handleInline drives nearly all those calls via self.inlinePatterns[patternIndex]. A tuple index is several times cheaper.
Precondition: The inline pattern registry is not modified while InlineProcessor.run executes; the new snapshot API on Registry (for example a method returning the sorted values list) is allowed to be added.
What the relaxed rule changes: Output is identical when patterns are not mutated during a conversion. Users who registe
red patterns dynamically from inside a pattern handler would see the change take effect only on the next convert call.
title: Cache a plain list of sorted inline patterns instead of indexing the Registry per step

rationale:
Change run's work stack to carry each element's ancestor tag list (already computed for the parent plus the element's own lowercased tag) so __build_ancestors need not walk the parent_map to the root for every popped element. The stack entries' semantic changes: the ancestors argument given to run would then be consumed as the base list directly.
Why it should win: __build_ancestors runs 16.5k times at about 2% self and walks to the root each time, calling tag.lower() per level; the parent alrea

dy stacks self.ancestors[:] when pushing children, so the chain is known.
Precondition: Elements inserted by inline processing are always attached with parent_map entries consistent with the stack's parents, and ancestors passed to run represent the tree's outer context.
What the relaxed rule changes: Ancestor lists are the same as those computed by the walk, so exclusion decisions and output are identical; only the private stack tuple format changes.
